name: Banaue and Batad
tagline: Two-thousand-year-old rice terraces carved by hand into the Cordillera mountains, a green amphitheatre of stone walls and water.
highlight: The amphitheatre of Batad's terraces, seen from the viewpoint after a walk through the mountain.
shortDescription: The Ifugao rice terraces, a UNESCO cultural landscape, with the Banaue viewpoint, the amphitheatre of Batad, Tappiya Falls, village trekking and Ifugao culture.
metaDescription: A Banaue and Batad travel guide: the Ifugao rice terraces, Batad amphitheatre, Tappiya Falls, Bangaan and Cambulo, hiking, Ifugao culture, how to get there from Manila, where to stay and a three-day plan.
budget: US$40–80 per day, budget to mid-range

image.alt: The Banaue rice terraces climbing the green mountain slopes

intro: In the Cordillera Mountains of northern Luzon, the Ifugao people have shaped whole mountainsides into stepped rice paddies, held by stone or mud walls, watered by a network of channels from the forest above. Built over about 2,000 years, and still farmed by hand, the Ifugao Rice Terraces are a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and often called the eighth wonder of the world, although the phrase is a promotional one.

Banaue is the gateway town, with terrace views from the town viewpoints, an Ifugao museum and guesthouses. The most spectacular terraces are at Batad, an hour and a half by jeepney and then a 30-minute walk from the road, where the terraces form a giant amphitheatre around a small village, with a trek to Tappiya Falls. Other terrace clusters include Bangaan, Hapao and Cambulo.

The area is remote, cool in the mornings and misty, and best explored on foot. Many visitors combine Banaue with Sagada, another mountain destination, and it is an eight- to nine-hour overnight bus trip from Manila. Planting season, from February to April, and the golden harvest from May to June, offer contrasting scenery.

whyVisit.intro: The rice terraces are one of the most impressive human landscapes in Asia.
